claims.subject: Linear 128 MiB organization
claims.finding: Two 64 MiB dies expose linear byte addresses 00000000 through 07FFFFFF; die boundary 04000000 is derived from organization.

claims.subject: JEDEC and IQ identity
claims.finding: Selected non-DTR IQ device ID is EF4021; IQ has fixed QE=1. This is not the IM/DTR policy.

claims.subject: Compatible opcode path
claims.finding: In flash 4-byte mode, 6B/32/20/D8 carry four address bytes and match the nRF QSPI hardware opcode family; B7 enables that flash mode.

claims.subject: ADDRCONF can transmit EN4B
claims.finding: Controller ADDRCONF supports an address-mode instruction and optional WIPWAIT/WREN. Reset opcode B7 does not mean it is sent: reset MODE is NoInstr.

claims.subject: Setting controller 32-bit addressing alone qualifies all 128 MiB
claims.finding: Address-mode coherence and dual-die state handling remain separate requirements; a controller address-width setting is not evidence of either firmware correctness or hardware qualification.

claims.subject: Per-die state and command classes
claims.finding: BUSY/SUS are independent. SR1/SR2/SR3, UID and SFDP follow die context. Several addressless commands are common to both dies; concurrent SR writes require both idle.

claims.subject: C2 instruction existence and transport shape
claims.finding: Datasheet lists C2 plus a Die ID byte. Linux v6.17 emits C2 with one output byte, no address or dummy phase, and uses indices 0 and 1 for this two-die capacity; select_die adds no WREN.

claims.subject: Complete C2 and WEL semantics
claims.finding: Exact-part vendor rules for die selection during BUSY/SUS, selection persistence, inter-command timing, and WEL effects on both dies have not been obtained. Linux behavior is useful corroboration, not the missing complete specification.
claims.remaining_action: Obtain/read AN0000035 or equivalent complete written Winbond clarification and validate the pinned implementation.

claims.subject: AN0000035 full text
claims.finding: Official catalog/search listing confirms title, v1.0, 2023-08-03 and contact-us access. Searches and official endpoint did not yield the full note in this audit; it was not read.
claims.remaining_action: Secure the exact applicable note; do not claim it is globally unavailable merely because retrieval failed.

claims.subject: Linux independent ready polling
claims.finding: For EF4021, Linux installs a readiness callback that selects each die and polls SR, with n_dice derived as capacity divided by 64 MiB.

claims.subject: Target SDK and dual-die policy
claims.finding: No target SDK/driver SHA is pinned in the project. Inspected Zephyr main polls one SR1 in qspi_wait_while_writing and lacks an explicit die loop/C2 implementation; nrfx busy_check also polls one status.
claims.remaining_action: Pin SDK/bootloader commits and implement/review explicit dual-die control under one lock before hardware qualification.

evidence.locator: qspi_wait_while_writing 467-485; configure_chip 611-683; no die or 0xc2 text found

claims.subject: Default Zephyr QE configuration is automatically correct for IQ
claims.finding: Binding default S1B6 is not IQ's fixed SR2.QE policy. Configuration must be explicit and must not write an unrelated status bit.
claims.remaining_action: Evaluate explicit NONE for automatic QE mutation, separately assert both SR2.QE values, and verify pinned driver behavior. Do not persistently write status as a workaround.

claims.subject: C2 is transportable on nRF52840
claims.finding: Opcode plus one data byte fits normal single-line custom instruction. Long-frame mode also exists; transport capability does not implement dual-die state policy.

evidence.locator: Sending custom instructions; Long frame mode; CINSTRCONF.LENGTH

claims.subject: Page and read alignment constraints
claims.finding: Selected datasheet has 256-byte pages and a 4-byte-aligned read-start note. DMA buffer constraints must also be satisfied in the chosen SDK.

evidence.locator: qspi_xfer DMA-accessible and word-aligned buffer checks 105-119

claims.subject: Continuous read through die boundary
claims.finding: W1 describes sequential access to the entire memory, and no explicit 64 MiB read-termination mandate was found. Split reads may be a conservative first-driver policy, not a proven mandatory chip limit.
claims.remaining_action: Compare split and continuous reads through 04000000 with full-address patterns and native transfer limits; enable only qualified behavior.

claims.subject: ADS versus ADP
claims.finding: ADS reports current address mode; nonvolatile ADP determines power-up/reset mode and defaults to zero. EN4B and controller configuration need a coherent initialization and warm-reset contract.

claims.subject: Resetting the MCU proves that external Flash has returned to POR state
claims.finding: An MCU-only reset does not establish a Flash supply cycle or a Flash reset command. WSON8 IQ has no independent dedicated RESET line to provide that guarantee.
claims.remaining_action: Boot must discover BUSY/SUS/DPD/address mode and safely synchronize without destructive reset of an ongoing operation.

claims.subject: Software-reset sequence and data risk
claims.finding: 66 then 99, with no intervening command, resets volatile settings. Datasheet warns that resetting ongoing/suspended program or erase can corrupt data and calls for BUSY/SUS checks first.

claims.subject: DPD is distinct from POR
claims.finding: B9 enters deep power-down; AB releases it after its timing requirement. Winbond's Serial NOR FAQ says status registers remain unchanged after AB. AB must not be treated as resetting ADS to its POR default.

evidence.locator: Status Register values after Release Power-down ABh

claims.subject: Complete two-die DPD and reset behavior
claims.finding: Exact selector/context behavior after DPD/wake, reset, mixed-busy broadcasts and incomplete POR remains unqualified for the target firmware.
claims.remaining_action: Resolve vendor semantics and run warm-reset, DPD and measured power-fault cases on both dies.

claims.subject: QSPI READY after erase means durable data/session completion
claims.finding: Nordic documents erase READY as operation-start notification. Completion of both dies and application-level record commit must be handled separately; DMA completion is not a session durability guarantee.

evidence.locator: qspi_erase 554-608 includes a separate status wait

claims.subject: QSPI signal integrity and supported speed
claims.finding: nRF52840 offers up to 32 MHz, but neither this audit nor DRC qualifies A1 signal integrity, supply transients or timing margin. No operating clock is declared physically qualified.
claims.remaining_action: Run full-image CRC and electrical measurements across chosen clocks and supported supply/temperature conditions under acquisition/BLE load.

evidence.locator: QSPI main features; high-drive GPIO configuration

claims.subject: UID dummy-byte ambiguity in extracted text
claims.finding: The extracted instruction table and detailed UID description do not give an unambiguous matching dummy-field count. No vendor-document contradiction is asserted without checking the original rendered figure.
claims.remaining_action: Inspect original figure and applicable revision, obtain clarification if needed, and capture the actual UID transaction on the prototype.

claims.subject: Recovery and journal correctness
claims.finding: Append-only blocks, CRC and separate commits are proposed architecture, not implemented or proven protection against interruption. Flash timeout means outcome uncertain until verified.
claims.remaining_action: Implement the memory layer and journal, define repeated-page-program rules, and run both-die power-cut tests through every data/metadata/erase phase.

claims.subject: Valid Flash voltage throughout write/erase and power-fail recovery
claims.finding: The selected part requires 2.7–3.6V operating VCC. Nominal 3.0V supply, MCU reset threshold or lower internal write-inhibit VWI do not prove that VCC stays valid through an ongoing operation.
claims.remaining_action: Qualify actual Flash-pin voltage, power-fail policy and interrupted-operation journal behavior together with the power audit.

datasheet_timing_reference.locator: 7.3 page 75 and 7.6 page 79; recheck for actual supply lot revision before implementation

proposed_architecture_not_implemented.bounds_check: offset <= capacity && length <= capacity - offset, before narrowing types
proposed_architecture_not_implemented.split_reads_at_die_boundary: conservative initial policy; not asserted mandatory by datasheet
proposed_architecture_not_implemented.application_journal: append-only, CRC32C, separate commit and redundant metadata; needs implementation and power-cut qualification

coverage: full 128 MiB CRC and no aliasing

release_blockers: Obtain AN0000035 or equivalent exact-part vendor clarification for all unresolved two-die control semantics.
Pin actual SDK, driver and bootloader revisions and review their code/configuration and applicable errata.
Implement coherent 4-byte addressing and explicit dual-die status/recovery policy without default QE misconfiguration.
Execute and record full 128 MiB boundary/CRC/erase/reset/DPD/power-cut/electrical qualification.
